scope: Fix round 2 answers the independent review's three findings. It re-runs no gap check; it makes read-only observations for the incident record and edits receipt text.

checks.name: pid-366-data-dir
checks.expectation: pid 366 (dagu server, no arguments) resolves the default Dagu home, so its data directory is $HOME/.local/share/dagu/data, the directory the accidental scheduler wrote.
checks.criteria: Confirmed if (a) /proc/366/environ has no DAGU_HOME/DAGU_DATA_DIR-type override and no XDG_DATA_HOME/XDG_CONFIG_HOME pointing elsewhere, AND (b) /proc/366/fd or /proc/366/maps or lsof shows at least one open path under $HOME/.local/share/dagu or $HOME/.config/dagu, OR the server's config file resolves there. Refuted if an override points elsewhere or its open files are under a different home. Inconclusive otherwise. Only the names and values of variables whose name matches DAGU_*HOME*, DAGU_*DIR*, DAGU_*PATH*, DAGU_*CONFIG*, XDG_*, HOME are printed; no other variable value is read into output (credential rule). Detection: an override would appear as a matching variable; a different home would show as open paths outside the default tree.

checks.name: birth-times-all-28
checks.expectation: Most of the 17 paths without a recorded birth time predate 23:22:40 (they are directories the server created earlier); a few created by the scheduler-only code paths (for example notifications/*, incidents/* subdirectories) may have been born at 23:22:42.
checks.criteria: `stat -c '%w %y %n'` on every one of the 28 paths from the incident's find list. A path counts as created by the accidental scheduler if its birth time is in [23:22:40, 23:26:00]; as pre-existing if earlier; unknown if %w is '-' or the path is gone. Detection: %w is filesystem birth time (ext4 statx), so a path created in the window shows a birth time in the window.

checks.name: no-live-writes
checks.expectation: No write to the live store in this round.
checks.criteria: Only stat, ls, ps, readlink, cat of /proc/366/{cmdline,maps} and a filtered environ read. No removal: the leave/remove decision is recorded as pending for the coordinator or user, with the observations it needs.
